THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: Demand describes the quantities buyers are willing and able to purchase at different prices, holding other demand conditions constant. Quantity demanded is the amount buyers choose at one particular price. The law of demand states that a lower own price increases quantity demanded and a higher own price decreases it, all else equal. An own-price change causes movement between points on the same demand curve; it does not shift the curve.

WATCH OUT

runs.text: A common mistake is to call every change in quantity a shift in demand. If the good's own price changes and buyers move from one point to another on the same demand curve, quantity demanded changes. Demand itself shifts only when a nonprice determinant changes.

transcript.sourceText: On the gourmet-donut graph, point A shows a price of $10 and quantity demanded of 100 thousand. Point B shows a lower price of $5 and quantity demanded of 225 thousand. Because both points lie on the same demand curve and only the good's own price changes, the move from A to B is an increase in quantity demanded of 125 thousand, not an increase in demand.
